physics.scenario: A trolley is released from rest at a mark on a ramp, runs down onto a level runway and passes through a light gate on the level runway. A card of length L on the trolley interrupts the beam; an electronic timer records the time t for which the beam is blocked. The run is repeated seven times.
principles: Average speed = distance ÷ time (A.1): the card of length L passes the gate in time t, so v = L/t
assumptions: The light gate is on the level runway, where the trolley moves at a constant velocity (friction is negligible over the 10 cm of the card), so L/t is its speed at the gate
The trolley is released from rest at the same mark each time
The timer starts and stops exactly when the card's edges cross the beam
derivation: The card moves its own length L while the beam is blocked: t = L/v, so v = L/t̄ from the mean time

v.note: speed at the gate after rolling down a gentle ramp

gate-time.statement: t = L/v (speed = distance / time; the speed is taken as constant while the card passes the gate)

text.stem:
A student releases a trolley from rest at a mark on a ramp. The trolley runs down the ramp onto a level runway, where it moves through a light gate. A card of length $L = (10.0 \pm 0.1)\ \text{cm}$ fixed to the trolley blocks the light beam, and a timer records the time $t$ for which the beam is blocked.

The student repeats the run seven times. The results are shown in the table.

diagram.alt: Side view: a ramp with a release mark near its top leads down onto a level runway. A trolley with a card on top moves along the level runway towards a light gate standing beside the runway; a dot on the gate marks the light beam, at the height of the card.
diagram.caption: The trolley is released down the ramp and travels through the light gate.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Identify the trial that should not be used in the analysis. Justify your answer using the data.
markscheme: It is about 0.025 s shorter than the mean of the other trials, much more than their spread (they lie within about $\pm 0.002\ \text{s}$ of each other) ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Suggest one cause of this reading that is consistent with its value.
markscheme: The time is too short, so the trolley was moving faster than in the other runs: for example it was released from above the mark, or it was pushed as it was released ✓

parts.label: c
parts.question: Calculate the mean time $\bar{t}$ of the remaining trials.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Determine the absolute uncertainty in $\bar{t}$, using the spread of the remaining readings.
markscheme: Half the range of the remaining readings: $\pm 0.0020\ \text{s}$ (accept 0.002 s) ✓

parts.label: e
parts.question: Determine the speed $v$ of the trolley as it passes through the light gate.

mistakes.feedback: Convert the card length to metres before dividing.

parts.label: f
parts.question: State and explain the effect on the value of $v$ if trial 5 had been included.
markscheme: The mean time would be smaller, so $v$ would be larger (by about 2 %) and would not represent a release from the mark ✓
